assigned.title: Catalog ingestion is scheduled and stored, not re-run per query
assigned.acceptance: Catalog answers are served from stored ingested state refreshed on a schedule, rather than by running a full ingestion pass per query. TODAY THE ADAPTER RUNS ONE FULL runIngestionPass PER QUERY, which is correct for a seam and wrong for a deployment: it makes every page view an outbound crawl, ties response time to an upstream service, and scales the load on that service with this product's traffic. Required: the freshness and next-pass planning PL-0305 already built is what DRIVES the schedule rather than being recomputed alongside it; an answer still carries its age and stated staleness policy, so nothing becomes fresher by being cached; tombstones survive a refresh, because a work withdrawn upstream must not reappear from stored state; a refresh that fails leaves the previous state served AND SAYS SO, rather than emptying the catalog or silently serving stale data as current; and rights and availability are re-evaluated against stored records rather than trusted from the pass that stored them, since a rights basis can lapse. The reviewer noted that PL-0305 is NOT to be described as having delivered a deployed ingestion worker; this task is where that claim would become true.
assigned.notes: Created 2026-09-20 on gpt-architect's round-52 direction when it approved PL-0305: 'Make sure the existing handoff has explicit ownership for ... If any is currently only prose with no task, create a narrow task before it can be forgotten.' PL-0305 is NOT to be reopened for any of these. Follow-up 2 of 4. Point 8 of the round-52 verdict. CORRECTIVE SURFACE AMENDMENT 2026-09-22, GRANTED BY gpt-architect at 9dc9bc8e1169092b30edf6e37128d489878ed237 and NOT self-taken. allowedPaths were ["packages/catalog-ingestion/**","apps/web/src/lib/catalog-ingestion-source.ts","apps/web/src/lib/catalog-ingestion-source.test.ts","packages/persistence/**","docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md"] and exactly three entries were added: ["apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts","apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.test.ts",".env.example"]. The reviewer's own words: 'This is not speculative widening. These are the production composition/configuration files required to satisfy PL-0309's existing acceptance.' The lead had declined to widen on its own judgement and put the choice to the reviewer, because PL-0308's verdict said in terms not to redesign server-bootstrap.ts or its runtime wiring, and because that file is where PL-0308's implementer proved the lead's own declared path wrong from Next 16.3.1's findPagesDir source. THREE ENTRIES AND NO MORE: .env.example is added for item 4 and is not a licence to touch other configuration. The package-level architecture is explicitly OUT OF BOUNDS for this corrective -- CatalogStore, applyPassToSnapshot, refreshCatalogIfDue and the accepted scheduler logic are not to be redesigned -- and policy_not_stated must REMAIN the behaviour for a runtime that intentionally omits a policy, so the corrective adds a stated policy to production composition rather than removing the unstated path.

typecheck.evidence: CORRECTIVE RE-RUN. npx turbo run typecheck --force, exit 0, 11 of 11; build --force, exit 0, 11 of 11; lint --force, exit 0, 11 of 11. RUN AS THREE SEPARATE INVOCATIONS THIS ROUND RATHER THAN ONE, AND THAT IS A PROCEDURE CHANGE WORTH RECORDING: the implementer hit a single unexplained @liberty/web#typecheck exit 2 with no error TS line, which passed on re-run twice. The structural cause was then verified rather than guessed -- apps/web/tsconfig.json includes .next/types/**/*.ts at line 15, turbo.json's build task writes .next/** as an output, and the typecheck task declares dependsOn ["^typecheck"] with no edge to build. So tsc and next build race on that directory whenever the two tasks run in one graph, which is exactly what the lead's own gate command has been doing for several rounds. It has passed every time until now, which is what a race looks like. This is PRE-EXISTING at HEAD and is NOT caused by PL-0309; neither turbo.json nor apps/web/tsconfig.json is on this task's surface and neither was touched. Reported for a ruling rather than fixed. ALSO RUN: npm run env:validate, passed, 22 declared variables with 3 pre-existing unrelated warnings; test:scripts 0 (38 environment, 69 control-plane, 16 validate-repo groups, 35 dispatcher); repo:validate 0. WHAT CHANGED: three names on CATALOG_SOURCE_ENV_VARS (LIBERTY_CATALOG_FRESH_FOR_MS, LIBERTY_CATALOG_STALE_AFTER_MS, LIBERTY_CATALOG_MAX_BACKOFF_MS), a schedule field on CatalogSourceDeclaration, a milliseconds() reader that decides only whether the value is a safe integer, a call to the package's validateCatalogRefreshSchedule, and schedule: declaration.schedule on the runtime the composition root returns. packages/catalog-ingestion/** and packages/persistence/** were both on the surface and were NOT changed: CatalogStore, applyPassToSnapshot, refreshCatalogIfDue and the accepted scheduler logic are untouched, as the verdict required.

unit.evidence: CORRECTIVE RE-RUN. npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2719 passed 1 skipped against the 2712/1 this task's previous round established: +7, all in server-bootstrap.test.ts, which went 16 tests to 23 (five schedule tests plus the two-part item-6 regression); @liberty/web 901 to 908. The lead recomputed the sum from the per-package figures rather than taking the implementer's table: 100+67+68+47+208+252+373+260+288+148+908 = 2719. ITEM 6 IS THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS AND THE LEAD RE-VERIFIED IT BY MUTATION. Deleting `schedule: declaration.schedule` from the runtime the composition root returns -- the single line that is the whole corrective, and exactly the defect the verdict named -- fails THREE tests: 'carries the operator's stated policy onto the registered runtime', 'asks the source once and serves the second read from stored state', and 'asks the source twice when the runtime states no policy at all'. 3 failed, 20 passed. So the regression is load-bearing in both directions rather than only the happy one. WHAT THE REGRESSION DRIVES: the real bootstrapCatalogMetadataSource, the real registry, resolveCatalogMetadataSource called PER READ rather than hoisted, the real adapter, scheduler, per-runtime store and ingestion pass. The only substitution is fetchImpl, through the transport parameter the composition root already exposes; the egress gate, classifyHost and address pinning in front of it are the real ones. Measured contrast, two reads one second apart with freshForMs 60000: with the schedule stated, ONE fetchImpl call, second read attempted:false, servedFromStoredState:true, scheduleReason 'state_fresh', freshness 'fresh' against the operator's own policy; with the schedule removed, TWO calls and 'policy_not_stated' on both reads with freshness null. THE COUNT ALONE WOULD PROVE LESS THAN IT LOOKS and the test knows it: a second read that threw, was backed off, or returned nothing would also fetch nothing, so it additionally asserts the second read SERVED an answer deep-equal to the first, and asserts 'state_fresh' rather than 'backing_off' -- a failed first pass also suppresses the second fetch, and would have made a naive version of this test pass for the wrong reason. TWO LIMITATIONS STATED BY THE IMPLEMENTER AND KEPT. First, the policy_not_stated half cannot go through bootstrapCatalogMetadataSource, because after this change no environment produces an unscheduled runtime -- which is the point of the corrective; it is built from the same catalogRuntimeFor output with the schedule removed by destructuring and registered through the same registry, so the two rows differ in exactly one field, and the test header says it is one step short of the real bootstrap. Second, the scripted row is refused as record_failed_validation rather than rights_basis_not_declared, because noRightsBasisEstablished answers null and ingestedWorkSchema rejects a work with no rights block before checkRightsBasis runs; verified by probe rather than assumed, and stated in the fixture comment.

architecture-review.evidence: FAIL, recorded by gpt-architect against origin 9dc9bc8e1169092b30edf6e37128d489878ed237. THE PACKAGE-LEVEL ARCHITECTURE IS ACCEPTED: CatalogStore is a valid port; applyPassToSnapshot centralizes stored-state transition semantics; refresh, backoff and freshness decisions are centralized rather than recomputed independently; failed refreshes retain previous state and record the failure; tombstones survive refreshes; refreshCatalogIfDue belongs in the package and is the right reusable worker entry point; and the per-runtime store identity mechanism prevents reconstructed sources from discarding state. THE FAIL IS THE DEPLOYMENT LEVEL AND NOTHING ELSE. apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts constructs CatalogIngestionRuntime without a schedule. Because schedule is optional that correctly becomes policy_not_stated, but the runtime then refreshes on every read, so a hosted deployment still performs the exact behaviour PL-0309 exists to remove: ingestion work scales with catalog reads instead of with a stated refresh schedule. architecture-review remains FAIL until production composition explicitly supplies the scheduling policy. PROVENANCE: TRANSCRIBED BY CLAUDE from the ChatGPT review session and relayed by the human commander; the GitHub review-write integration returns 403.

rights-review.evidence: PASS, recorded by gpt-architect against origin 9dc9bc8e1169092b30edf6e37128d489878ed237. Evidence: stored state contains accepted/ingested work rather than frozen projected catalog answers; the rights basis is rechecked at read time; availability is re-evaluated at read time; a stored record whose rights basis is no longer established is withheld; tombstoned works are not silently restored by a partial refresh; failed refreshes preserve previously stored state rather than clearing it; and the cache/store cannot turn stale authorization into current entitlement. No blocking rights defect found. The reviewer stated that rights-review MAY REMAIN PASS after the corrective if the corrective does not alter rights handling, so this record is re-examined rather than assumed on the next round. PROVENANCE: TRANSCRIBED BY CLAUDE from the ChatGPT review session and relayed by the human commander; the GitHub review-write integration returns 403.

review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED by gpt-architect at origin 9dc9bc8e1169092b30edf6e37128d489878ed237. architecture-review FAIL, rights-review PASS; both recorded as gates. The package-level architecture is accepted in full and MUST NOT BE REDESIGNED: CatalogStore, applyPassToSnapshot, refreshCatalogIfDue and the accepted scheduler logic are explicitly out of bounds for the corrective. The FAIL is the deployment level only: production composition does not supply a scheduling policy, so a hosted deployment still scales ingestion work with catalog reads. CORRECTIVE SURFACE RULING, granted by the reviewer and not self-taken: add EXACTLY apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts, apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.test.ts and .env.example, on the stated ground that this is not speculative widening but the production composition and configuration files required to satisfy PL-0309's EXISTING acceptance. SIX REQUIRED ITEMS: (1) production bootstrap constructs the catalog runtime with an explicit refresh schedule; (2) the schedule uses PL-0309's existing scheduling and freshness vocabulary rather than duplicating cadence or backoff arithmetic in apps/web; (3) scheduling policy is operator-stated, never silently defaulted; (4) .env.example documents the deployment configuration; (5) policy_not_stated REMAINS the honest behaviour for runtimes that intentionally omit policy, so it is not to be removed; (6) a real-bootstrap regression proves a configured deployment serves stored state WITHOUT running a full ingestion pass on every catalog read. After the corrective, re-run typecheck, unit and architecture-review; rights-review may remain PASS if the corrective does not alter rights handling. SEPARATE FOLLOW-UP ORDERED: a task for the resume/full-pass tombstone invariant, before resume support is enabled -- a resumed pass can reach the provider's end having intentionally skipped earlier pages, and if that is treated as a complete full-source observation then known ids from the skipped pages could be inferred absent and mass-tombstoned. The follow-up must make "complete" mean the whole source was observed for absence inference rather than merely that this invocation reached end-of-enumeration. It does not block PL-0309 today because the current scheduler does not resume. PROVENANCE: TRANSCRIBED BY CLAUDE from the ChatGPT review session and relayed by the human commander; the GitHub review-write integration returns 403.

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests
